docs.title: GoGoogle
docs.text: Go libraries for Google APIs - higher-level utilities built on the official Google API Go Client.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
GoGoogle provides simplified, production-ready interfaces for common Google API operations:

Package Description Gmail Send emails, manage messages, mail merge Docs Extract content from Google Docs Sheets Read/write spreadsheet data with typed structs Slides Create presentations, add content Search Console Read Search Console properties, search performance, sitemaps and URL inspection Maps Generate static map images Speech Speech-to-Text and Text-to-Speech Forms OAuth scope helpers for Forms API YouTube URL utilities (short URLs) CLI Command-line tools for Google APIs

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Simplified APIs - Higher-level functions for common operations
  • Type Safety - Go structs for API data
  • Batch Operations - Efficient bulk processing
  • Mail Merge - Template-based email campaigns with Sheets integration
  • OAuth2 Support - Built-in authentication helpers

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: go get github.com/grokify/gogoogle

docs.title: Send an Email
docs.text:
import (
    "context"
    "github.com/grokify/gogoogle/gmailutil/v1"
)

// Create Gmail service (after OAuth setup)
service, _ := gmailutil.NewGmailService(ctx, httpClient)

// Send a simple email
service.SendSimple(ctx, "me", gmailutil.SendSimpleOpts{
    To:       "recipient@example.com",
    Subject:  "Hello from GoGoogle",
    BodyText: "This is a test email.",
    BodyHTML: "<p>This is a <b>test</b> email.</p>",
})

docs.title: Design
docs.text:
How the packages are put together, and why.

  • Architecture describes the structure of the library.
  • Architecture Decisions records decisions that are costly to reverse, one record each.

docs.title: Architecture Decisions
docs.text:
Each record states a decision, its context and its consequences. Records are numbered in the order they were written and are not renumbered.

There are no records yet.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
GoGoogle is a set of independent packages over the official Google API Go Client. Each package is named <name>util and carries its API version in the import path, for example gmailutil/v1 or searchconsoleutil/v1.

  • Each package takes an authorized *http.Client or builds one from credentials, so the caller chooses how people or services sign in.
  • Packages wrap the generated client in types and functions for common tasks and return errors that carry the underlying Google error.
  • Packages do not depend on each other.

Package guides are under Guides.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
GoGoogle uses OAuth2 for authentication. You'll need:

  1. A Google Cloud project with APIs enabled
  2. OAuth2 credentials (client_secret.json)
  3. User authorization (generates token.json)

docs.title: Enable Google APIs
docs.text:
1. Go to Google Cloud Console
  2. Create or select a project
  3. Enable the APIs you need:
  4. Gmail API
  5. Google Sheets API
  6. Google Slides API
  7. etc.

docs.title: Create OAuth Credentials
docs.text:
1. Go to APIs & Services > Credentials
  2. Click Create Credentials > OAuth client ID
  3. Select Desktop app as application type
  4. Download the JSON file as client_secret.json

docs.title: Authorize Your Application
docs.text:
Use goauth for OAuth2 flow:

import (
    "context"
    "github.com/grokify/goauth/google"
)

client, err := google.NewClientOAuthCLITokenStore(google.ClientOAuthCLITokenStoreConfig{
    Context:   ctx,
    AppConfig: clientSecretJSON,  // Contents of client_secret.json
    Scopes:    []string{
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/gmail.send",
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets.readonly",
    },
    TokenFile: "token.json",      // Will be created after authorization
    State:     "my-app",
})
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

On first run, this opens a browser for user authorization. The token is saved to token.json for subsequent runs.

docs.title: CLI Tools

docs.title: Installation

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Command Description gmail merge Send templated emails via mail merge gmail send-markdown Send email with markdown body slides content Extract content from presentations

docs.title: Gmail: Mail Merge
docs.text:
Send templated emails using Google Sheets data:

gogoogle gmail merge \
    --credentials client_secret.json \
    --token token.json \
    --sheet-id "1abc123..." \
    --subject-template templates/subject.mustache \
    --html-template templates/body.html.mustache \
    --text-template templates/body.txt.mustache

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Flag Description --credentials OAuth credentials file --token Token file path --sheet-id Google Sheets ID --sheet-name Sheet name (default: first sheet) --subject-template Subject template file --html-template HTML body template file --text-template Plain text template file --inline Inline image (format: cid:path) --attachment File attachment path --from From address (default: "me")

docs.title: Example with Inline Images
docs.text:
gogoogle gmail merge \
    --sheet-id "1abc123..." \
    --subject-template "Newsletter - {{date}}" \
    --html-template templates/newsletter.html.mustache \
    --inline "logo:images/logo.png" \
    --inline "banner:images/banner.jpg" \
    --attachment "documents/terms.pdf"

docs.title: Gmail: Send Markdown
docs.text:

gogoogle gmail send-markdown \
    --credentials client_secret.json \
    --token token.json \
    --to recipient@example.com \
    --subject "Meeting Notes" \
    --body @notes.md

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Flag Description --credentials OAuth credentials file --token Token file path --from From address (default: "me") --to Recipient address --cc CC recipients (comma-separated) --bcc BCC recipients (comma-separated) --subject Email subject --body Body text or @filename

docs.title: Google Docs Utilities
docs.text: The docsutil/v1 package provides utilities for working with the Google Docs API.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: import docsutil "github.com/grokify/gogoogle/docsutil/v1"

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Client wrapper - Simplified Google Docs API client
  • Content extraction - Extract structured content (headings, paragraphs, images, tables)
  • Text extraction - Get plain text or paragraph-by-paragraph text
  • URL parsing - Extract document IDs from Google Docs URLs

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "log"
    "net/http"

    docsutil "github.com/grokify/gogoogle/docsutil/v1"
)

func main() {
    ctx := context.Background()

    // Create client with authenticated HTTP client
    client, err := docsutil.NewClient(ctx, httpClient)
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    // Get document by ID or URL
    docID := docsutil.ParseDocumentID("https://docs.google.com/document/d/DOC_ID/edit")

    // Extract all content
    content, err := client.ExtractContent(ctx, docID, docsutil.ExtractOptions{
        IncludeImages: true,
        IncludeTables: true,
    })
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatal(err)
    }

    fmt.Printf("Title: %s\n", content.Title)
    for _, section := range content.Sections {
        fmt.Printf("[%s] %s\n", section.Type, section.Text)
    }
}

docs.title: ExtractContent
docs.text:
Returns structured content including headings, paragraphs, images, and tables.

content, err := client.ExtractContent(ctx, docID, docsutil.ExtractOptions{
    IncludeImages:  true,
    IncludeTables:  true,
    IncludeHeaders: true,
    IncludeFooters: true,
})

Returns:

  • Title - Document title
  • Sections - Array of content sections with type, level, and text
  • Images - Array of image info (if requested)
  • Tables - Array of table data (if requested)
  • Headers - Array of header text (if requested)
  • Footers - Array of footer text (if requested)

docs.title: ExtractText
docs.text:
Returns all document text as a single string.

text, err := client.ExtractText(ctx, docID)

docs.title: ExtractParagraphs
docs.text:
Returns text organized by paragraphs.

paragraphs, err := client.ExtractParagraphs(ctx, docID)
for _, p := range paragraphs {
    fmt.Println(p)
}

docs.title: Suggestions
docs.text:
Reviewers' suggested edits do not appear in a normal fetch. Fetch the document with suggestions shown inline, then split the text into what was there, what would be added, and what would be removed:

doc, err := svc.GetDocumentWithSuggestions(ctx, docID, "SUGGESTIONS_INLINE")
if err != nil {
    return err
}
sc := docsutil.ExtractSuggestionContent(doc)
for _, b := range sc.Blocks {
    fmt.Printf("%s\n  was: %q\n  if accepted: %q\n", b.Location, b.Original, b.Accepted)
}
  • Every paragraph and table cell is a block, with a Location such as body/p/12 or body/table/2/r/3/c/1.
  • Each block has segments of kind original, insertion, or deletion, in document order, with the suggestion IDs that affect them.
  • Original is the original and deletion text; Accepted is the original and insertion text.
  • The Docs API does not report who made a suggestion, so blocks carry no author. Comments do; see the Drive guide.

From the command line: gogoogle docs suggestions <documentID|URL>.

docs.title: URL Parsing
docs.text:
Parse document IDs from various Google Docs URL formats:

// Standard edit URL
id := docsutil.ParseDocumentID("https://docs.google.com/document/d/DOC_ID/edit")

// URL with query parameters
id := docsutil.ParseDocumentID("https://docs.google.com/document/d/DOC_ID/edit?tab=t.0")

// URL with anchors
id := docsutil.ParseDocumentID("https://docs.google.com/document/d/DOC_ID/edit#heading=h.xyz")

// Just the ID
id := docsutil.ParseDocumentID("DOC_ID")

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
The client requires an authenticated *http.Client. Use goauth for OAuth2 setup:

import "github.com/grokify/goauth/google"

// Service account
httpClient, err := google.NewClientSvcAccountFromFile(ctx, "credentials.json",
    "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/documents.readonly",
)

// OAuth2 user credentials
httpClient, err := google.NewClientFromTokenFile(ctx, "token.json")

docs.title: Required Scopes
docs.text:
• https://www.googleapis.com/auth/documents.readonly - Read-only access
  • https://www.googleapis.com/auth/documents - Full access

docs.title: Google Drive
docs.text: The driveutil/v3 package uploads local files to Drive, optionally converting them to Google Docs, Sheets, or Slides, replaces the content of an existing file, and lists a file's comments. Together with the suggestion-aware Docs extraction and the Sheets records reader, it supports a review round trip: publish a document, let people comment and suggest edits, and read their responses back as data.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: go get github.com/grokify/gogoogle/driveutil/v3

docs.title: Create the service
docs.text:
import driveutil "github.com/grokify/gogoogle/driveutil/v3"

svc, err := driveutil.NewService(ctx, httpClient)
if err != nil {
    return err
}

httpClient is any authorized *http.Client. Extra option.ClientOption values, such as option.WithEndpoint, follow the client.

docs.title: Upload with conversion
docs.text:
f, err := svc.Upload(ctx, driveutil.UploadRequest{
    Path:      "review.docx",
    FolderID:  folderID, // optional
    ConvertTo: driveutil.ConvertDoc,
})
// f.ID, f.Name, f.MimeType, f.WebViewLink, f.ModifiedTime, f.HeadRevisionID
ConvertTo Accepted extensions Result ConvertDoc .docx, .odt, .txt, .html Google Doc ConvertSheet .csv, .xlsx, .ods Google Sheet ConvertSlides .pptx, .odp Google Slides file ConvertNone (empty) any stored unchanged

An extension that does not match the target returns an error wrapping ErrUnsupportedConversion. When converting, the file name defaults to the base name without its extension.

sheetsutil.CreateFromCSV(ctx, svc, "data.csv", "", folderID) is a shortcut for a CSV-to-Sheet upload.

docs.title: Update in place
docs.text:
f, err := svc.Update(ctx, fileID, "review-v2.docx", driveutil.ConvertDoc)

The file ID, link, sharing, and comments are kept, so reviewers keep working in the same document.

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
comments, err := svc.ListComments(ctx, fileID, driveutil.ListCommentsOptions{})
for _, c := range comments {
    fmt.Println(c.QuotedText, c.Content, c.Resolved, len(c.Replies))
}

Each comment has the text it is anchored to (QuotedText), its author, its resolved state, and its replies. Paging is followed to the end: you get every comment or an error, never a partial list. Author email addresses appear only when the API returns them; treat them as personal data.

docs.title: Suggested edits
docs.text:
Comments do not include suggested edits. Fetch the document with its suggestions shown inline and split the text:

doc, err := docsSvc.GetDocumentWithSuggestions(ctx, docID, "SUGGESTIONS_INLINE")
sc := docsutil.ExtractSuggestionContent(doc)
for _, b := range sc.Blocks {
    fmt.Println(b.Location, b.Original, "->", b.Accepted)
}

See the Docs guide.

docs.title: Structured responses in a Sheet
docs.text:
For answers that need a fixed shape, publish a CSV as a Sheet and read it back:

records, err := sheetsutil.ReadRecords(ctx, sheetsSvc, sheetID, "") // first sheet
// []map[string]string keyed by the header row

See the Sheets guide.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
gogoogle drive upload review.docx --convert doc --folder 1AbC
gogoogle drive update 1FileId review-v2.docx --convert doc
gogoogle drive comments 1FileId --include-deleted
gogoogle docs suggestions 1DocId
gogoogle sheets records 1SheetId --sheet "Round 1"

All commands print JSON. Exit status is 0 on success, 1 for an API or input error, and 2 for a usage error.

docs.title: Scopes
docs.text:
Use the narrowest scope that works.

Operation Scope Upload, update drive.file (files this app creates or opens) List comments drive.readonly Read suggestions documents.readonly Read records spreadsheets.readonly

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Failures wrap the operation and the resource ID. ErrNotFound (HTTP 404), ErrPermissionDenied (HTTP 403), and ErrUnsupportedConversion work with errors.Is; the underlying *googleapi.Error works with errors.As. Retries are left to the caller's HTTP client.

docs.title: Gmail
docs.text: The gmailutil/v1 package provides utilities for Gmail API operations.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Send emails - Simple and advanced message composition
  • Read messages - List, filter, and retrieve emails
  • Batch operations - Delete multiple messages efficiently
  • Mail merge - Send templated emails using Google Sheets data
  • Label management - List and manage Gmail labels

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
import (
    "context"
    "net/http"
    "github.com/grokify/gogoogle/gmailutil/v1"
)

// Create Gmail service
func getGmailService(ctx context.Context, httpClient *http.Client) (*gmailutil.GmailService, error) {
    return gmailutil.NewGmailService(ctx, httpClient)
}

docs.title: SendSimple (Recommended)
docs.text:
The simplest way to send emails:

_, err := service.SendSimple(ctx, "me", gmailutil.SendSimpleOpts{
    To:       "recipient@example.com",
    Subject:  "Hello",
    BodyText: "Plain text body",
    BodyHTML: "<p>HTML body</p>",  // Optional
    ReplyTo:  "replies@example.com", // Optional
})

docs.title: Send with MessageWriter
docs.text:
For more control over email composition:

import "github.com/grokify/mogo/net/mailutil"

msg := mailutil.MessageWriter{
    To:      mailutil.Addresses{{Address: "recipient@example.com"}},
    Subject: "Hello",
    // ... additional fields
}

_, err := service.Send(ctx, "me", msg)

docs.title: Mail Merge
docs.text: Send templated emails to multiple recipients using Google Sheets as the data source.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Mail merge allows you to:

  • Define email templates with Mustache placeholders
  • Pull recipient data from Google Sheets
  • Send personalized emails at scale
  • Include inline images and attachments

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
import "github.com/grokify/gogoogle/gmailutil/v1/mailmerge"

mm := mailmerge.MailMerge{
    GmailService: gmailService,
    SheetsService: sheetsService,
    SpreadsheetID: "your-spreadsheet-id",
    SubjectTemplate: "Hello {{name}}!",
    BodyHTMLTemplate: "<p>Dear {{name}}, your order #{{order_id}} is ready.</p>",
    BodyTextTemplate: "Dear {{name}}, your order #{{order_id}} is ready.",
}

err := mm.Execute(ctx)

Column Required Description TO Yes Recipient email address CC No CC recipients BCC No BCC recipients * No Any other columns become template variables

docs.title: SendSimple
docs.text:
The SendSimple method provides the easiest way to send emails:

import "github.com/grokify/gogoogle/gmailutil/v1"

service, _ := gmailutil.NewGmailService(ctx, httpClient)

_, err := service.SendSimple(ctx, "me", gmailutil.SendSimpleOpts{
    To:       "recipient@example.com",
    Subject:  "Meeting Tomorrow",
    BodyText: "Let's meet at 2pm.",
    BodyHTML: "<p>Let's meet at <b>2pm</b>.</p>",
    ReplyTo:  "replies@mycompany.com",
})

docs.title: SendSimpleOpts
docs.text: Field Type Description To string Recipient email address Subject string Email subject line BodyText string Plain text body (required) BodyHTML string HTML body (optional, creates multipart) ReplyTo string Reply-To header (optional)

docs.title: Text Only vs HTML
docs.text:
// Text only
opts := gmailutil.SendSimpleOpts{
    To:       "user@example.com",
    Subject:  "Plain Text Email",
    BodyText: "This is plain text.",
}

// Text + HTML (multipart/alternative)
opts := gmailutil.SendSimpleOpts{
    To:       "user@example.com",
    Subject:  "Rich Email",
    BodyText: "This is the plain text fallback.",
    BodyHTML: "<h1>Rich Email</h1><p>This is HTML content.</p>",
}

docs.text:

import (
    "github.com/grokify/mogo/net/mailutil"
    "github.com/grokify/gogoogle/gmailutil/v1"
)

msg := mailutil.MessageWriter{
    From:    mailutil.Address{Address: "sender@example.com", Name: "Sender Name"},
    To:      mailutil.Addresses{{Address: "recipient@example.com", Name: "Recipient"}},
    Cc:      mailutil.Addresses{{Address: "cc@example.com"}},
    Subject: "Hello",
    Header: map[string][]string{
        "X-Custom-Header": {"custom-value"},
    },
}

// Set body
msg.BodyPartsSet, _ = multipartutil.NewPartsSetMail(
    []byte("Plain text"),
    []byte("<p>HTML</p>"),
    nil, // attachments

_, err := service.Send(ctx, "me", msg)

docs.title: From Address
docs.text:
The from parameter specifies the sender:

// Send as authenticated user
service.SendSimple(ctx, "me", opts)

// Send as specific address (must have permission)

Use "me" to send from the authenticated user's primary address.

result, err := service.SendSimple(ctx, "me", opts)
if err != nil {

    default:

    return
}

docs.title: Google Maps
docs.text: The mapsutil/staticmap package generates Google Static Maps images.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Create map images with:

  • Custom center, zoom, and dimensions
  • Styled markers with colors and labels
  • Preset regions (USA, Europe, World)
  • Download as PNG files

docs.title: Quick Start

import "github.com/grokify/gogoogle/mapsutil/staticmap"

// Create a map centered on San Francisco
mapConfig := staticmap.MapConfig{
    Center:  "San Francisco, CA",
    Zoom:    12,
    Width:   600,
    Height:  400,
    MapType: "roadmap",
    APIKey:  os.Getenv("GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY"),

url := staticmap.BuildURL(mapConfig)
fmt.Println(url)

import "github.com/grokify/gogoogle/mapsutil/staticmap"

func createOfficeMap() error {
    offices := []staticmap.Marker{
        {Location: "San Francisco, CA", Color: "red", Label: "H"},    // HQ
        {Location: "New York, NY", Color: "blue", Label: "N"},
        {Location: "Austin, TX", Color: "blue", Label: "A"},
        {Location: "Seattle, WA", Color: "blue", Label: "S"},
    }

    mapConfig := staticmap.MapConfig{
        Center:   "United States",
        Zoom:     4,
        Width:    800,
        Height:   500,
        MapType:  "roadmap",
        Markers:  offices,
        APIKey:   os.Getenv("GOOGLE_MAPS_API_KEY"),
    }

    imageData, err := staticmap.Download(mapConfig)
    if err != nil {
        return err
    }

    return os.WriteFile("offices.png", imageData, 0644)
}

docs.title: Google Search Console
docs.text: The searchconsoleutil/v1 package reads Google Search Console: the properties a credential can see, search performance, sitemaps and URL inspection. It is read-only and requests only the webmasters.readonly scope.

docs.title: Connect with a service account
docs.text:
A service account lets a server read Search Console without a person signing in.

  1. In Google Cloud, enable the Google Search Console API and create a service account and a JSON key for it.
  2. In Search Console, open Settings, then Users and permissions, and add the service account's email as a user on each property it should read. The lowest permission that can read is enough.
  3. Create the client from the key:
import searchconsole "github.com/grokify/gogoogle/searchconsoleutil/v1"

key, err := os.ReadFile("key.json")
if err != nil {
    return err
}
email, _ := searchconsole.ServiceAccountEmail(key) // the address to add in step 2
c, err := searchconsole.NewFromServiceAccountKey(ctx, key)

The context is used each time the access token is refreshed, so pass one that lasts as long as the client. NewFromServiceAccountKey accepts only service account keys. To use credentials from another source, authorize an *http.Client for searchconsole.ScopeReadonly and pass it to searchconsole.New.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
sites, err := c.Sites(ctx)
for _, s := range sites {
    if s.CanRead() && s.MatchesDomain("example.com") {
        fmt.Println(s.URL, s.PermissionLevel, s.IsDomainProperty())
    }
}

A property is either a domain property, sc-domain:example.com, covering every subdomain and protocol, or a URL-prefix property such as https://www.example.com/. The URL is the identifier the other methods take. MatchesDomain is true when the property's host is the domain, a subdomain of it, or a parent domain that covers it.

docs.title: Search performance
docs.text:
end := time.Now().AddDate(0, 0, -3) // Search Console holds data back for days
start := end.AddDate(0, 0, -27)

totals, err := c.Totals(ctx, site, start, end)       // clicks, impressions, CTR, position
daily, err := c.Daily(ctx, site, start, end)         // one row per day, oldest first
queries, err := c.Top(ctx, site, searchconsole.DimensionQuery, start, end, 25)
pages, err := c.Top(ctx, site, searchconsole.DimensionPage, start, end, 25)

Query is the general form, with dimensions, filters, a search type, a data state and paging:

res, err := c.Query(ctx, site, searchconsole.Query{
    Start: start, End: end,
    Dimensions: []searchconsole.Dimension{searchconsole.DimensionQuery, searchconsole.DimensionDevice},
    Filters: []searchconsole.Filter{{
        Dimension: searchconsole.DimensionPage, Operator: searchconsole.FilterContains, Expression: "/blog/",
    }},
    RowLimit: 100,
})
fmt.Println(res.FirstIncompleteDate) // data from this date may still change

Only the calendar date of a time.Time is used. Search Console reports dates in Pacific time.

docs.title: Sitemaps and URL inspection
docs.text:
maps, err := c.Sitemaps(ctx, site)

in, err := c.InspectURL(ctx, site, "https://example.com/pricing")
fmt.Println(in.Indexed(), in.CoverageState, in.LastCrawl, in.GoogleCanonical)

URL inspection is limited per property per day, so cache what it returns.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Failed API calls wrap both a sentinel and the underlying *googleapi.Error:

Error Meaning ErrUnauthorized Google rejected the credentials ErrForbidden The credentials cannot access the property, for example the service account was not added to it ErrNotFound The property, sitemap or URL does not exist for the credentials ErrQuotaExceeded A rate or daily quota was reached 
if errors.Is(err, searchconsole.ErrForbidden) {
    // ask the owner to add the service account to the property
}

docs.title: Google Sheets
docs.text: The sheetsutil package provides utilities for reading and writing Google Sheets data.

docs.title: Packages
docs.text: Package Description sheetsutil/v4 Cell value parsing, URL utilities, header-keyed records, and CSV-to-Sheet upload sheetsutil/v4/sheetsmap Map sheet data to Go types with validation sheetsutil/iwark Low-level operations using Iwark library

docs.title: Records
docs.text:
Create a service with sheetsutil.NewService(ctx, httpClient); its SheetsService field is the underlying *sheets.Service. ReadRecords takes that service:

Read a sheet as records keyed by its header row:

records, err := sheetsutil.ReadRecords(ctx, svc.SheetsService, spreadsheetID, "Round 1")
// [{"id": "el-1", "response": "agree"}, ...]
  • An empty sheet name reads the first sheet.
  • Values are the formatted text shown in the sheet.
  • Columns with a blank header are ignored, short rows are padded with empty strings, and rows with no values are skipped.
  • A repeated header returns an error wrapping ErrDuplicateHeader.

Publish a CSV as a new Sheet with sheetsutil.CreateFromCSV, which uploads through the Drive package.

From the command line: gogoogle sheets records <spreadsheetID|URL> [--sheet NAME].

docs.title: Cell Value Parsing
docs.text:
Parse Google Sheets API responses into typed Go structures:

import sheetsutil "github.com/grokify/gogoogle/sheetsutil/v4"

// Get values from Sheets API
vr, _ := service.Spreadsheets.Values.Get(spreadsheetID, "Sheet1!A1:D10").Do()

// Parse to typed grid - each cell has type information
grid := sheetsutil.ParseValueRange(vr)
for _, row := range grid {
    for _, cell := range row {
        fmt.Printf("Type: %s, Value: %s\n", cell.Type, cell.FormattedValue)
    }
}

// Or extract as simple strings
formatted := sheetsutil.ExtractFormattedValues(vr)  // Display values
raw := sheetsutil.ExtractRawValues(vr)               // Underlying values

docs.title: Cell Types
docs.text: Type Description CellTypeEmpty Empty cell CellTypeString Text value CellTypeNumber Numeric value CellTypeBool Boolean (TRUE/FALSE) CellTypeDate Date value CellTypeTime Time value CellTypeDateTime Date and time CellTypeDuration Duration CellTypeError Error value

docs.title: URL Utilities
docs.text:
Parse spreadsheet IDs from URLs and build URLs:

import sheetsutil "github.com/grokify/gogoogle/sheetsutil/v4"

// Extract spreadsheet ID from URL or plain ID
id, err := sheetsutil.ParseSpreadsheetURL(
    "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/abc123/edit#gid=0",
)
// id = "abc123"

// Extract full info including sheet GID and range
info, err := sheetsutil.ParseSpreadsheetURLFull(
    "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/abc123/edit#gid=456&range=A1:D10",
)
// info.SpreadsheetID = "abc123"
// info.SheetGID = 456
// info.Range = "A1:D10"

// Build URLs from ID
url := sheetsutil.BuildSpreadsheetURL("abc123")
// "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/abc123/edit"

url := sheetsutil.BuildSpreadsheetURLWithSheet("abc123", 456)
// "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/abc123/edit#gid=456"

// Check if string is a Sheets URL
if sheetsutil.IsSpreadsheetURL(input) {
    // Handle URL
}

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
import (
    "context"
    "google.golang.org/api/sheets/v4"
    "google.golang.org/api/option"
)

// Create Sheets service
service, err := sheets.NewService(ctx, option.WithHTTPClient(httpClient))
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

// Read spreadsheet
spreadsheetID := "1BxiMVs0XRA5nFMdKvBdBZjgmUUqptlbs74OgvE2upms"
readRange := "Sheet1!A1:D10"

resp, err := service.Spreadsheets.Values.Get(spreadsheetID, readRange).Do()
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

for _, row := range resp.Values {
    fmt.Println(row)
}

docs.title: sheetsmap
docs.text:
Map spreadsheet data to typed Go structures:

import "github.com/grokify/gogoogle/sheetsutil/v4/sheetsmap"

// Define your data structure
type Contact struct {
    Name  string
    Email string
    Phone string
}

// Read and map data
data, err := sheetsmap.ReadSpreadsheet(ctx, service, spreadsheetID, "Contacts")
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

// Access rows as maps
for _, row := range data.Rows {
    name := row["Name"].(string)
    email := row["Email"].(string)
    fmt.Printf("%s: %s\n", name, email)
}

docs.text:
// Define column mappings
columns := sheetsmap.Columns{
    {Name: "Name", Required: true},
    {Name: "Email", Required: true, Validator: sheetsmap.ValidateEmail},
    {Name: "Status", Enum: []string{"active", "inactive", "pending"}},
}

// Read with validation
data, err := sheetsmap.ReadSpreadsheetWithColumns(ctx, service, spreadsheetID, "Sheet1", columns)

columns := sheetsmap.Columns{
    {
        Name: "Priority",
        Enum: []string{"low", "medium", "high", "critical"},
    },
    {
        Name: "Status",
        Enum: []string{"open", "in_progress", "resolved", "closed"},
    },
}

docs.title: Writing Data
docs.text:
// Prepare values
values := [][]interface{}{
    {"Name", "Email", "Phone"},
    {"John Doe", "john@example.com", "555-0100"},
    {"Jane Smith", "jane@example.com", "555-0101"},
}

// Write to sheet
_, err := service.Spreadsheets.Values.Update(
    spreadsheetID,

docs.title: Speech-to-Text
docs.text: The speechtotext package provides a wrapper for Google's Speech-to-Text API.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Transcribe audio from bytes or files
  • Multiple language support
  • Confidence threshold filtering
  • Word-level timestamps

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
import (
    "context"
    "os"
    "github.com/grokify/gogoogle/speechtotext"
)

// Read audio file
audioData, _ := os.ReadFile("audio.wav")

// Transcribe
result, err := speechtotext.Transcribe(ctx, httpClient, speechtotext.TranscribeRequest{
    Audio:        audioData,
    LanguageCode: "en-US",
    Encoding:     "LINEAR16",
    SampleRate:   16000,
})
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}

fmt.Println(result.Transcript)

docs.title: TranscribeRequest
docs.text: Field Type Description Audio []byte Audio data LanguageCode string BCP-47 language code Encoding string Audio encoding SampleRate int Sample rate in Hz MinConfidence float64 Minimum confidence (0-1)

docs.title: Audio Encodings
docs.text: Encoding Description LINEAR16 Uncompressed 16-bit PCM FLAC FLAC encoded MULAW μ-law encoded AMR AMR (Adaptive Multi-Rate) AMR_WB AMR Wideband OGG_OPUS Ogg Opus MP3 MP3 encoded

docs.title: Language Codes
docs.text:
Common language codes:

Language Code English (US) en-US English (UK) en-GB Spanish es-ES French fr-FR German de-DE Japanese ja-JP Chinese (Mandarin) zh-CN Portuguese (Brazil) pt-BR

docs.title: Transcription Result
docs.text:
type TranscribeResult struct {
    Transcript  string    // Full transcript
    Confidence  float64   // Overall confidence (0-1)
    Words       []Word    // Word-level results
}

type Word struct {
    Word       string
    StartTime  time.Duration
    EndTime    time.Duration
    Confidence float64
}

docs.title: Confidence Filtering
docs.text:
result, err := speechtotext.Transcribe(ctx, httpClient, speechtotext.TranscribeRequest{
    Audio:         audioData,
    LanguageCode:  "en-US",
    MinConfidence: 0.8, // Only include high-confidence results
})

docs.title: File Transcription
docs.text:
result, err := speechtotext.TranscribeFile(ctx, httpClient, "audio.wav", speechtotext.TranscribeRequest{
    LanguageCode: "en-US",
})

docs.title: Long Audio
docs.text:
For audio longer than 1 minute, use async recognition:

operation, err := speechtotext.TranscribeAsync(ctx, httpClient, speechtotext.AsyncTranscribeRequest{
    AudioURI:     "gs://bucket/audio.wav", // GCS URI
    LanguageCode: "en-US",
})

// Poll for completion
result, err := speechtotext.WaitForResult(ctx, httpClient, operation)

docs.text: scope := "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"

docs.title: Enable API
docs.text:
1. Go to Google Cloud Console
  2. Enable Cloud Speech-to-Text API
  3. Create service account or OAuth credentials

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use appropriate encoding - LINEAR16 for highest accuracy
  2. Set correct sample rate - Must match audio
  3. Specify language - Don't rely on auto-detection
  4. Use GCS for long audio - Required for files > 1 minute

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
result, err := speechtotext.Transcribe(ctx, httpClient, request)
if err != nil {
    switch {
    case strings.Contains(err.Error(), "INVALID_ARGUMENT"):
        log.Println("Invalid audio format or parameters")
    case strings.Contains(err.Error(), "RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED"):
        log.Println("Quota exceeded")
    default:
        log.Printf("Transcription error: %v", err)
    }
}

import (

import sheetsutil "github.com/grokify/gogoogle/sheetsutil/v4"

id, err := sheetsutil.ParseSpreadsheetURL("https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/abc123/edit#gid=0")

info, err := sheetsutil.ParseSpreadsheetURLFull("https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/abc123/edit#gid=456&range=A1:D10")
// info.SpreadsheetID = "abc123"

// Build URLs
url := sheetsutil.BuildSpreadsheetURL("abc123")
// url = "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/abc123/edit"

Adds searchconsoleutil/v1, a read-only client for Google Search Console that signs in with a service account. Nothing is breaking.

docs.text:
• New searchconsoleutil/v1 package for Google Search Console
  • Service account sign-in that requests only the read-only scope
  • Search performance, sitemaps and URL inspection in typed results
  • Errors that tell unauthorized, forbidden, not found and quota failures apart

docs.title: Search Console client
docs.text:
import searchconsole "github.com/grokify/gogoogle/searchconsoleutil/v1"

c, err := searchconsole.NewFromServiceAccountKey(ctx, key)
sites, err := c.Sites(ctx)
totals, err := c.Totals(ctx, site, start, end)
  • Properties. Sites lists the properties a credential can see and tells domain properties from URL-prefix ones. MatchesDomain finds the properties that cover a domain.
  • Search performance. Totals, Daily and Top cover the common readings. Query is the general form, with dimensions, filters, search type, data state and paging. Results report the date from which data may still change.
  • Indexing. Sitemaps lists a property's sitemaps. InspectURL returns how Google indexed one page, and Indexed() answers the common question.
  • Credentials. NewFromServiceAccountKey accepts only service account keys and requests only webmasters.readonly. ServiceAccountEmail returns the address to add as a user on each property. New takes any authorized *http.Client.
  • Errors. Failed calls wrap a sentinel (ErrUnauthorized, ErrForbidden, ErrNotFound, ErrQuotaExceeded) and the underlying Google error, so both errors.Is and errors.As work.

docs.text:
Release Date: 2026-10-30

Adds what a document review round trip needs: upload a file to Drive and convert it, replace its content in place, and read back the comments, the suggested edits, and a Sheet of structured responses. Nothing is breaking.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
• New driveutil/v3 package: upload with conversion, update in place, comments
  • Suggested edits split into original, inserted, and deleted text
  • Sheets read as records keyed by the header row; a CSV published as a Sheet
  • gogoogle drive, docs suggestions, and sheets records commands

docs.title: Drive: upload, update, and comments
docs.text:
import driveutil "github.com/grokify/gogoogle/driveutil/v3"

svc, err := driveutil.NewService(ctx, httpClient)
f, err := svc.Upload(ctx, driveutil.UploadRequest{Path: "review.docx", ConvertTo: driveutil.ConvertDoc})
f, err = svc.Update(ctx, f.ID, "review-v2.docx", driveutil.ConvertDoc)
comments, err := svc.ListComments(ctx, f.ID, driveutil.ListCommentsOptions{})
  • Conversion. .docx, .odt, .txt, and .html become Google Docs; .csv, .xlsx, and .ods become Sheets; .pptx and .odp become Slides files. A mismatched extension returns ErrUnsupportedConversion.
  • Update in place. The file ID, link, sharing, and comments are kept.
  • Comments. Each comment has its quoted text, author, resolved state, and replies. Listing returns every page or an error, never a partial result.

docs.title: Docs: suggested edits
docs.text: docsutil.ExtractSuggestionContent takes a document fetched with SUGGESTIONS_INLINE and returns one block per paragraph and table cell, each split into original, insertion, and deletion segments, with the original and as-if-accepted text of the block. The Docs API does not report who made a suggestion, so blocks carry no author.

docs.title: Sheets: records and CSV
docs.text: sheetsutil.NewService creates a Sheets service, like the Drive and Docs services, so callers need not import the Google client packages directly. It reads ranges with GetValues and BatchGetValues. The Slides service gains GetPresentation. sheetsutil.ReadRecords reads a sheet as []map[string]string keyed by the header row. sheetsutil.CreateFromCSV publishes a CSV file as a Sheet.

docs.text:
gogoogle drive upload review.docx --convert doc
gogoogle drive update <fileID> review-v2.docx --convert doc
gogoogle drive comments <fileID>
gogoogle docs suggestions <documentID>
gogoogle sheets records <spreadsheetID> --sheet "Round 1"

Output is JSON. Exit status is 0 on success, 1 for an API or input error, and 2 for a usage error.

See the Drive guide.

docs.title: PRD — Document review round trip — Drive upload and conversion, comments, and suggestion-aware Docs content
docs.text: Initiative: INIT-GOGOOGLE-001 Repository: github.com/grokify/gogoogle Workflow: pbhq-lite Status: Draft — pending stakeholder review (pbhq-lite gate: after PRD)

docs.title: 1. Problem
docs.text:
A common workflow is to generate a document or deck from structured data, share it in Google Drive for people to review, and then read their responses back into the source system. gogoogle covers parts of this today:

  • Read Docs, Sheets, and Slides. docsutil, sheetsutil, and slidesutil read native Google files.
  • Fetch with suggestions inline. docsutil.GetDocumentWithSuggestions can fetch a document in SUGGESTIONS_INLINE mode.

Three gaps block the round trip:

  1. No Drive package. There is no way to upload a .docx, .pptx, or .csv with conversion to a native Google Doc, Slides, or Sheet, or to replace a file's contents with a new version while keeping its ID and sharing. Reviewers therefore get files that the Docs, Sheets, and Slides APIs cannot read, and every revision becomes a new link.
  2. Comments are invisible. Reviewers mostly respond with comments. Comments live in the Drive API (comments.list), not the Docs API, so no gogoogle function returns them, along with the text they anchor to, their replies, or whether they are resolved.
  3. Suggestions are flattened. ExtractDocumentContent concatenates text runs without looking at suggestedInsertionIds or suggestedDeletionIds. A document read in suggestions-inline mode returns original text, suggested insertions, and suggested deletions mixed together, so a consumer cannot tell what a reviewer proposed.

Who is affected:

  • Go applications that publish documents for review.
  • MCP servers and agents built on gogoogle (they can expose only what gogoogle provides).
  • CLI users who want a scriptable upload and review read.

Desired state: with one library and CLI, a caller can:

  • upload with conversion;
  • update in place;
  • list comments with their anchors;
  • read a Doc as segments marked original, suggested insertion, or suggested deletion;
  • create a Sheet from CSV and read it back as records.

docs.title: 2.1 Goals
docs.text: ID Goal Success criterion G-1 Publish files for review as native Google files Upload of .docx → Doc, .pptx → Slides, .csv/.xlsx → Sheet returns file ID and web link; tests cover each conversion's request G-2 Revise without breaking links Update-in-place replaces content of an existing file ID; ID and permissions unchanged G-3 Read comments with context Every comment returns author display name, created/modified time, content, quoted anchor text, resolved flag, and replies; all pages fetched G-4 Read suggestions faithfully Suggestion-aware extraction distinguishes original text, suggested insertions, and suggested deletions (with suggestion IDs), for paragraphs and table cells G-5 Review sheets as data Create a Sheet from CSV and read any sheet as header-keyed records G-6 Scriptable from the CLI gogoogle drive upload\|update\|comments, gogoogle docs suggestions, gogoogle sheets records emit JSON

docs.title: 2.2 Non-Goals
docs.text:
• Writing comments, replying, or resolving them.
  • Accepting or rejecting suggestions.
  • Sharing / permission management (callers share via Drive UI or existing tools).
  • Drive search, folder sync, or storage abstractions.
  • Rendering or converting Markdown (callers produce .docx/.pptx/.csv).
  • Authentication changes beyond requesting the needed Drive scopes.

docs.title: 3. User Stories
docs.text:
US-1 — Publish for review. As an application developer, I want to upload a generated .docx as a Google Doc into a given folder, so that reviewers can comment and suggest in Google Docs. Acceptance: driveutil.Upload(ctx, UploadRequest{Path, Name, FolderID, ConvertTo: Doc}) returns File{ID, Name, MimeType, WebViewLink}; a request test asserts the target MIME type application/vnd.google-apps.document.

US-2 — Publish a new version. As an application developer, I want to replace an existing reviewed file's contents with a new version, so that reviewers keep the same link. Acceptance: driveutil.Update(ctx, fileID, path, convertTo) keeps the file ID; a request test asserts a media update on the existing ID.

US-3 — Read reviewer comments. As an application or agent, I want all comments on a file with the text they refer to, so that each response can be matched to the part of the document it concerns. Acceptance: driveutil.ListComments(ctx, fileID, opts) returns all pages; fields include QuotedText, Resolved, Author, Replies; deleted comments are excluded unless requested.

US-4 — Read proposed edits. As an application or agent, I want a document's suggested insertions and deletions separated from its original text, so that I can propose the same edits to my source of truth. Acceptance: docsutil.ExtractSuggestionContent(doc) over a fixture with insertions and deletions in a paragraph and a table cell yields segments with Kind ∈ {original, insertion, deletion} and suggestion IDs.

US-5 — Review in a sheet. As an application developer, I want to create a review sheet from CSV and later read the edited sheet as records, so that structured responses (agree / change / comment per row) come back as data. Acceptance: CSV upload converts to a Sheet; sheetsutil.ReadRecords returns []map[string]string keyed by the header row, skipping empty rows.

US-6 — Do it from the shell. As a CLI user, I want commands for the above, so that scripts and AI agents can drive the round trip. Acceptance: CLI tests cover argument validation and JSON output shape.

docs.title: 4. Functional Requirements
docs.text:
• PRD-FR-1 driveutil/v3 MUST provide a service constructed like the other gogoogle packages (from an *http.Client), and GetFile returning ID, name, MIME type, web link, modified time, and head revision ID.
  • PRD-FR-2 Upload MUST support conversion targets Doc, Sheet, Slides, and no conversion; an optional parent folder; and return the created file.
  • PRD-FR-3 Update MUST replace the media of an existing file ID, with the same conversion rules, and return the updated file.
  • PRD-FR-4 Comment listing MUST page through all results and return author, times, content, quoted anchor text, resolved flag, deleted flag, and replies (author, time, content, action such as resolve / reopen).
  • PRD-FR-5 Suggestion-aware extraction MUST walk body paragraphs and table cells of a document fetched with SUGGESTIONS_INLINE and return ordered segments with kind and suggestion IDs, plus a convenience view of each paragraph / cell as original and as-if-accepted text.
  • PRD-FR-6 Sheets: create from CSV (via Drive conversion) and ReadRecords(spreadsheetID, sheetName) keyed by the header row.
  • PRD-FR-7 CLI commands per G-6, JSON to stdout, errors to stderr, non-zero exit on failure.
  • PRD-FR-8 Existing APIs MUST remain backward compatible; new behavior is additive.

  • Permission management and sharing.
  • Native Google Slides generation improvements in slidesutil.
  • MCP / agent tool surfaces (these live in wrapper projects that import gogoogle).

docs.title: 1. Introduction
docs.text:
Purpose. Specify the new driveutil/v3 package, suggestion-aware extraction in docsutil/v1, record helpers in sheetsutil/v4, and CLI commands for a document review round trip.

Scope. Library and CLI only; see PRD non-goals.

References. PRD · PLAN · ROADMAP · Google Drive API v3 (files.create, files.update, files.get, comments.list) · Google Docs API v1 (documents.get, suggestionsViewMode).

  • INV-2 Every API call takes a context.Context; errors are wrapped with the operation and resource ID and returned, never logged-and-dropped.
  • INV-3 Listing functions return either all pages or an error — never a silent partial result.
  • INV-4 Suggestion extraction preserves document order; concatenating original + deletion segments yields the original text, and original + insertion segments yields the as-if-accepted text.

caller ─► driveutil/v3  ──► Drive API v3 (files, comments)

docs.title: 6.4 Suggestion-aware Docs extraction
docs.text:
type SegmentKind string // "original", "insertion", "deletion"
type Segment struct {
    Kind          SegmentKind `json:"kind"`
    Text          string      `json:"text"`
    SuggestionIDs []string    `json:"suggestion_ids,omitempty"`
}
type Block struct {
    Location string    `json:"location"` // "body/p/12" or "body/table/2/r/3/c/1"
    Segments []Segment `json:"segments"`
    Original string    `json:"original"` // original + deletion segments
    Accepted string    `json:"accepted"` // original + insertion segments
}
type SuggestionContent struct {
    DocumentID    string   `json:"document_id"`
    Blocks        []Block  `json:"blocks"`
    SuggestionIDs []string `json:"suggestion_ids"` // distinct, document order
}
func ExtractSuggestionContent(doc *docs.Document) *SuggestionContent

Fetching. Callers fetch the document with GetDocumentWithSuggestions(ctx, id, "SUGGESTIONS_INLINE").

Classification:

  • A text run with SuggestedInsertionIds → insertion.
  • A text run with SuggestedDeletionIds → deletion.
  • Any other run → original.

Grouping. Adjacent runs of the same kind and IDs are merged. Table cells are walked in row-major order. A block is emitted for every paragraph and cell, including blocks without suggestions, so callers can align blocks with ExtractDocumentContent output.

Authors. The Docs API does not expose suggestion authors, so Block carries none. Comments do carry authors.

docs.title: 12. Testing Strategy
docs.text:
• Fake servers. Unit tests use httptest servers with option.WithEndpoint and option.WithHTTPClient, recording requests to assert methods, MIME types, fields masks, and paging.
  • Suggestion fixtures. Suggestion extraction is tested against recorded documents.get JSON responses, plus a property test for INV-4.
  • Optional integration tests. These run behind GOGOOGLE_IT=1 and are never required in CI.

docs.title: 13. Deployment
docs.text: Released as a tagged minor version (v0.13.0) after CI is green; release notes list the new packages and functions. Rollback: callers pin v0.12.0.

docs.title: 14. Alternatives Considered
docs.text: Alternative Why rejected Read comments by exporting the file as .docx and parsing comment XML Loses resolved state and reply threading and needs a second parser; the Drive comments API is authoritative Return suggestions as raw docs.TextRun lists Leaves every caller to reimplement classification; the segment model with original and accepted views is what consumers need Implement these features inside MCP wrappers Wrappers should stay thin; other Go programs and the CLI need the same functions
